}}{{TIDTOC|embedded}} ==Overview== === FCC === Per FCC test report {{FCC.io|PY313200233}} (w/ ''Manual Tool v2.0.1.0'' as the utility), the device seems to be… * [[Broadcom]]-based, and * supported by a {{#ask:[[WI1 chip1 model::BCM4360]] OR [[WI2 chip1 model::BCM4360]]|limit=0|mainlabel=Device|searchlabel=BCM4360}}-powered WLAN AC card.
Netgear requested FCC re-certification for the R7000 on December 17, 2018 under {{FCC.io|PY318300420}} due to an internal redesign, likely as part of a drive to cut manufacturing costs. Some minor components (RAM, FEM, etc.) may have changed, but the same Broadcom chips are still used. :{{FCC ST|06/16/2019}}
=== Wi-Fi Alliance® === Netgear sought evaluation for two variants of the device shortly after launch and both received the CERTIFIED™ classification on March 7, 2014. * {{WiFiCert|WFA53679|03/05/2014|9323}} * {{WiFiCert|WFA53679|03/06/2014|20466}}
==Links of Interest== ===News=== * [https://www.smallnetbuilder.com/wireless/wireless-news/netgear-joins-the-ac1900-club/ ''NETGEAR Joins The AC1900 Club''] on '''SmallNetBuilder''' : [[Broadcom]] BCM4709A0 (''BCM4709A0KFEBG'') and a pair of BCM4360 :* There is a single USB 3.0 port on the front of the unit and another (though only USB 2.0) in the rear. :* This device seems to be functionally equivalent (or quite similar) to the [[ASUS RT-AC68U]].
